solutions.latex: There could be a point where fertiliser will not produce extra yield. Reasons could include: high volume of fertiliser may cause damage to the plant; other factors may limit yield, e.g. sunlight/water; plants may not be able to absorb fertiliser at that rate.

$y=3x-x^3-1$

$y'=3-3x^2$

$y''=-6x$

For stationary points, $y'=0$: $3-3x^2=0$, $x^2=1$, $x=\pm1$

$x=1$: $y=3\times1-1^3-1=1$; $y''=-6\times1=-6<0$

$\therefore(1,1)$ is a maximum turning point.

$x=-1$: $y=3\times(-1)-(-1)^3-1=-3$; $y''=-6\times-1=6>0$

$\therefore(-1,-3)$ is a minimum turning point.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution; 2: finds the coordinates of all the stationary points; 1: finds the correct values of $x$ for the stationary points

solutions.latex:
$y''=-6x$

$-6x=0$, so $x=0$

$y=3x-x^3-1=-1$

$\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&-1&0&1\\\hline y''&6&0&-6\\ &\cup&*&\cap\end{array}$

Since there is a change in concavity, $(0,-1)$ is a point of inflection.

solutions.latex:
From the graph, when $t=\dfrac\pi2$, maximum turning point for the velocity function, indicates acceleration is $0\text{ m/s}^2$.

OR

$\ddot x=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=8\sin2t$

$t=\dfrac\pi2$: $\ddot x=8\sin\pi=0\text{ m/s}^2$

$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2-4\cos2t$

$x=\displaystyle\int(2-4\cos2t)\,dt=2t-2\sin2t+C$

$t=0,\ x=3$: $3=0-2\sin0+C$, $C=3$

$x=2t-2\sin2t+3$

When $t=\pi$: $x=2\pi-2\sin2\pi+3=2\pi+3$

The displacement of this particle is $2\pi+3$ metres to the right of the origin when $t=\pi$.

Perimeter is $2h+2r+\pi r$

$16\pi=2h+2r+\pi r$

$2h=16\pi-2r-\pi r$

$h=8\pi-r-\dfrac12\pi r$

$A=2rh+\dfrac12\pi r^2$

$A=2r\left(8\pi-r-\dfrac{\pi r}{2}\right)+\dfrac{\pi r^2}{2}$

$A=16\pi r-2r^2-\pi r^2+\dfrac{\pi r^2}{2}$

$A=16\pi r-2r^2-\dfrac{\pi r^2}{2}$

$\dfrac{dA}{dr}=16\pi-4r-\pi r$

$\dfrac{dA}{dr}=0$: $16\pi-4r-\pi r=0$

$4r+\pi r=16\pi$

$r(4+\pi)=16\pi$

$r=\dfrac{16\pi}{4+\pi}$

$\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2}=-4-\pi<0$

$\therefore r=\dfrac{16\pi}{4+\pi}$ produces a maximum area.
